manuscript_prose.section1_title: Polyphyletic Origins of Mycorrhizal Symbiosis and Terrestrialization Across Fungi
section1_paragraphs: Mycorrhizal fungi form obligate and facultative root mutualisms with most extant vascular and non-vascular land plants, trading mineral phosphorus and ammonium for host photosynthates [5, 13]. Yet ectomycorrhizal (ECM), ericoid (ERM), arbuscular (AM), and fine-root endophyte guilds are distributed discontinuously across Glomeromycotina, Mucoromycotina, Ascomycota, and Basidiomycota [5, 6, 9, 10]. Evaluating whether plant-fungal biotrophy reflects single ancestral recruitment or repeated convergent innovation requires resolving deep fungal relationships across Paleozoic terrestrialization horizons [7, 8, 9].

Concatenated nuclear phylogenies across Holomycota remain susceptible to adenine-thymine compositional drift at third codon positions, rate heterogeneity across ribosomal versus housekeeping markers, and long-branch attraction between fast-evolving Chytridiomycota, Zoopagomycota, and budding yeasts [2, 3, 24]. Partitioned substitution modeling coupled with third-codon purine-pyrimidine (RY3) recoding and multi-locus quartet coalescent reconciliation directly addresses both compositional skew and deep incomplete lineage sorting [2, 4, 19, 24].

Here we present a multi-compartment phylogenomic synthesis across 64 fungal taxa stratified across basal Holomycota ([A]), Zoopagomycota ([B]), Glomeromycotina ([C]), Mucoromycotina and Mortierellomycotina ([D]), Ascomycota ([E]), non-ECM Basidiomycota ([F]), and Agaricomycotina ([G]). We couple a completeness-gated 23-locus nuclear supermatrix and 24-gene-tree quartet coalescent analysis with relaxed-clock calibration, 61-state codon selection on four symbiotic functional families (CHS1, MEP2, MST2, and PHO84/PiPT threaded onto PDB 4J05), and twelve single-species Pleistocene-to-modern coalescent skylines [1, 14, 15, 20, 21, 23].
manuscript_prose.section1_p1: Mycorrhizal fungi form obligate and facultative root mutualisms with most extant vascular and non-vascular land plants, yet their trophic associations originated repeatedly across distant fungal phyla [5, 9, 10].
manuscript_prose.section1_p2: Partitioned RY3 phylogenomics, 64-species quartet coalescent inference, transporter codon modeling, and conspecific skylines across 64 fungal taxa evaluate Paleozoic AM origins versus younger Dikarya symbiotic transitions [1, 14, 20].
manuscript_prose.section2_title: Twenty-Three-Locus Nuclear Supermatrix, RY3 Recoding, and Relaxed-Clock Chronogram
section2_paragraphs: Automated sequence validation across 489 verified public NCBI records (2,312,092 raw nucleotides) quarantined 3,833 spurious or reading-frame-disrupted accessions and assembled a 24-locus target design [1]. Because mitochondrial COX1 met coverage in only 7 taxa (below the 10-taxon partition floor), 23 universal nuclear loci (21 protein-coding markers under RY3 plus 18S SSU [1,674 bp] and 28S LSU [775 bp]) were retained across 43 species passing the 55% site and 10-locus completeness filter ([7, 5, 3, 8, 8, 5, 7] taxa across sectors [A]-[G]; L = 36,208 aligned columns, 27,063 site patterns, 23,984 parsimony-informative sites). Per-locus BIC model selection chose 16 GTR+F+I+G4, 5 GTR+F+G4, and 2 TN+F+I+G4 partitions with edge-linked proportional rates from 0.434x (RPL8/uL2) to 1.809x (MCM7) [2]. Compositional RY3 recoding lowered RCFV by 87.1% (0.0987 unrecoded and 0.0993 unphased control vs. 0.0127 RY3) [24], and partitioned modeling improved ML fit by Delta ln L = +5,836.89 nats (ln L = -678,788.85 vs. -684,625.73 unpartitioned; Delta BIC = -9,259.5; 32-chain thermodynamic marginal ln L = -678,433.64; MCMC ESS = 3,877.9, R-hat = 1.0001) with 86.9% mean Seo multilocus UFBoot2 support (B = 500) [3, 4].

Under an autocorrelated relaxed molecular clock with soft fossil priors and two-sided 95% highest posterior density intervals on all 42 internal vertices (Figure 1) [18], the Holomycota root (Node I) resolves at 967.2 Ma (876.2-1,048.7 Ma) and the Mortierellomycotina-Dikarya stem divergence (Node II) at 819.8 Ma (749.6-876.3 Ma). Crown Glomeromycotina arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi (Node III) diversify at 413.2 Ma (365.2-438.2 Ma), consistent with Ordovician glomalean spores and Lower Devonian Rhynie Chert symbioses [7, 8], whereas Mucoromycotina fine-root endophytes (Node IV) crown at 499.3 Ma (462.2-529.9 Ma) [5, 6]. Within Dikarya (Node V: 707.5 Ma [653.9-754.6 Ma]), Basidiomycota diverged at 577.7 Ma (Node VI: [538.7-619.6 Ma]), Pezizomycotina radiated at 397.7 Ma (Node VII: [366.0-427.5 Ma]), and crown Agaricomycetes ectomycorrhizal and wood-decay lineages (Node VIII) emerged at 267.2 Ma (252.6-307.6 Ma), preceding Middle Eocene Pinaceae ectomycorrhizal fossils [9, 10, 16].
manuscript_prose.section3_title: Sixty-Four-Taxon Quartet Multispecies Coalescent and Four-Taxon Discordance Tests
section3_paragraphs: To incorporate the 21 lower-coverage taxa omitted from concatenated tree inference and account for incomplete lineage sorting across ancient rapid splits, exact tripartition dynamic programming evaluated 3,244,416 quartets across all 24 nuclear gene trees (including EF1A/TEF1, Table 3C and Figure 3) [19]. Native quartet reconciliation achieved normalized Q = 0.7065 (2,292,225 satisfied quartets; mean LPP = 0.7329), outperforming Codon-12 (Q = 0.6987), unrecoded 4-state (Q = 0.7022), and unaligned controls (Q = 0.4709). Both partitioned RY3 ML (89-100% bootstrap) and 64-species quartet MSC (0.68-0.94 LPP) recovered 1.00 monophyly for Glomeromycotina, Mucoromycotina, Mortierellomycotina, Ascomycota, Basidiomycota, Agaricomycotina, Dikarya, and Pezizomycotina, while separating Mortierellomycotina from Glomeromycotina plus Mucoromycotina [5, 6].

At the focal backbone vertices in Table 2A, Glomeromycotina (Node III: q1 = 1.000, LPP = 0.8716), Basidiomycota (Node VI: q1 = 0.855, LPP = 0.7117), Pezizomycotina (Node VII: q1 = 0.790, LPP = 0.9739), and Agaricomycetes (Node VIII: q1 = 0.667, LPP = 0.8435) display strong primary quartet concordance, whereas Holomycota (Node I: q1 = 0.419, LPP = 0.4779, 0.14 CU) and Mucoromycotina (Node IV: q1 = 0.459, LPP = 0.5053, 0.21 CU) reflect rapid early radiation. Four-taxon Patterson D tests further detect asymmetric gene-tree discordance in Zoopagomycota-Mucoromycota (ABBA-1: D = -0.0653, Z = 1.95), Glomeromycotina-Mucoromycotina (ABBA-2: D = +0.8824, Z = 21.21), Ascomycota (ABBA-3: D = -0.0634, Z = 1.76), and Agaricomycotina (ABBA-4: D = +0.1708, Z = 5.32) [22].
manuscript_prose.section4_title: Goldman-Yang Codon Selection on PHO84/PiPT (PDB 4J05), MEP2, MST2, and CHS1 Symbiosis Genes
manuscript_prose.section4_body: Coding sequence alignments of fungal phosphate transporters, ammonium permeases, hexose symporters, and chitin synthases evaluate evolutionary constraint accompanying the transition to plant-root biotrophy.
section4_paragraphs: Frame-locked Goldman-Yang 61-state codon models across 42 curated fungal orthologs indicate pervasive purifying selection across symbiotic nutrient-exchange and cell-wall loci, with zero codons reaching Bayes Empirical Bayes posterior Pr >= 0.95 for positive diversifying selection (Figure 5A-B) [21]. Background M0 omega stays constrained in fungal chitin synthase CHS1/CHS2 (FAM-01: n = 11, 759 codons, omega0 = 0.0696, kappa = 1.22, purifying fraction omega0 = 0.0577 [85.7%]), symbiotic ammonium permease MEP2/AMT1 (FAM-02: n = 12, 477 codons, omega0 = 0.0660, kappa = 1.58, purifying omega0 = 0.0436 [95.4%]) [23], monosaccharide symporter HXT/MST2 (FAM-03: n = 11, 496 codons, omega0 = 0.1306, kappa = 1.06, purifying omega0 = 0.1315 [84.8%]) [15], and high-affinity H+-orthophosphate symporter PHO84/PiPT (FAM-04: n = 8, 425 codons, omega0 = 0.0770, kappa = 1.20, purifying omega0 = 0.0606 [96.6%]) [14].

Threading fungal PHO84/PiPT orthologs onto the 2.90 A crystal structure of Serendipita indica PiPT in its occluded orthophosphate-bound conformation (PDB 4J05 Chain A bound to PO4 A 600; 422 aligned C-alpha atoms; Kabsch RMSD = 0.424 A, TM-score = 0.9968; Figure 5D) preserves the twelve-helix major facilitator fold linking the TM1-TM6 N-domain (residues 31-228) and TM7-TM12 C-domain (298-518) [14]. Within the buried transport pocket (volume 137.8 cubic A, predicted binding affinity -2.29 kcal/mol), polar anchor Asn431 Nd2 maintains 3.39 A proximity to occluded PO4 A 600 alongside Gln177, Tyr150, and proton-relay residue Asp324, consistent with conserved transmembrane electrostatic geometry across distantly related mycorrhizal mutualists [14].
manuscript_prose.section5_title: Conspecific Mycorrhizal Population Skylines and Multi-Locus Haplotype Cluster Networks
section5_paragraphs: Twelve single-species 25,000-generation Bayesian coalescent skylines spanning 383 aligned fungal isolates across forestry, heathland, and agroecosystem populations converged robustly (minimum ESS = 1,886.2, maximum Gelman-Rubin R-hat = 1.0013; Figure 4A-B) [20]. Aggregate regime likelihoods in Table 3B place codon and E-INS-i core modeling first (ln L = -20,936.09; 91.7% mean bootstrap) ahead of progressive FFT-NS-i / K80+G4 (-21,291.16), untrimmed gotoh-msa (-21,966.75), and unaligned controls (-194,565.39). Across the R1-R6 regional ITS cohorts (N = 193; Rhizophagus irregularis, Funneliformis mosseae, Cenococcum geophilum, Suillus luteus, Amanita muscaria, and Tuber melanosporum), demographic curves show late-Pleistocene stability and recent expansion, whereas multi-compartment L1-L6 contrasts (N = 190) separate polymorphic nuclear ITS and 28S LSU (L2, pi = 0.0640) from completely invariant R. irregularis 18S SSU (L5: n = 36, 785 bp, pi = 0.0000).

Because multiple lineages exceeded three distinguishable genetic groups, minimum spanning haplotype cluster networks were constructed from single-species ITS alignments (Figure 7A-B). Global R. irregularis ITS isolates (Cohort R1: N = 20, 19 unique haplotypes, Hd = 0.9947, pi = 0.1083, maximum k-core = 2) partition into 12 discrete haplotype clusters (4 bounded clusters containing >=2 haplotypes separated by 9-101 mutational steps), compatible with co-existing divergent ribotypes in clonal and agricultural soils [13]. Circumpolar ectomycorrhizal Amanita muscaria ITS populations (Cohort R5: N = 28, 21 haplotypes, Hd = 0.9709, pi = 0.0120, maximum k-core = 2) segregate into 4 clusters (Clusters I-IV separated by 11-13 steps), mirroring boreal Pleistocene refugial sorting.
manuscript_prose.section6_intro: Empirical diagnostics, divergence times, clade recovery metrics, 32-chain sweeps, codon selection parameters, and conspecific population skyline budgets are compiled across Tables 1 through 4C.
discussion_paragraphs: **Paleozoic Arbuscular and Mucoromycotina Terrestrialization Versus Later Dikarya Guilds.** Relaxed-clock calibration places crown Glomeromycotina at 413.2 Ma (365.2-438.2 Ma) and crown Mucoromycotina at 499.3 Ma (462.2-529.9 Ma), temporally consistent with Ordovician glomalean microfossils, Lower Devonian Rhynie Chert symbioses in early embryophytes, and molecular plant-fungal co-diversification models [6, 7, 8, 9]. Separating Mortierellomycotina (stem split 819.8 Ma) from Glomeromycotina plus Mucoromycotina across both partitioned RY3 ML and quartet MSC topologies supports ancient trophic differentiation prior to Dikarya radiation at 707.5 Ma [5, 6].

**Convergent Ectomycorrhizal and Ericoid Evolution Alongside Decay-Enzyme Contraction.** Crown Agaricomycetes ECM and wood-rot lineages diversify at 267.2 Ma (252.6-307.6 Ma) within Permian-Mesozoic gymnosperm-dominated biomes, well before Middle Eocene Pinaceae ectomycorrhizal permineralizations (~48-50 Ma) [10, 16]. Together with Ascomycota ECM/ERM diversification nested inside Pezizomycotina (397.7 Ma [366.0-427.5 Ma]), these timing bounds are consistent with repeated, independent evolutionary transitions from saprotrophy to root biotrophy accompanied by convergent reductions in plant cell-wall-degrading enzymes [10, 11, 12].

**Purifying Constraint on Symbiotic Phosphate, Ammonium, Hexose, and Chitin Machinery.** Strong background purifying selection across CHS1/CHS2 (omega0 = 0.0696), MEP2/AMT1 (omega0 = 0.0660), HXT/MST2 (omega0 = 0.1306), and PHO84/PiPT (omega0 = 0.0770), with zero BEB sites >= 0.95 and sub-angstrom structural conservation (0.424 A RMSD) on PDB 4J05, supports a candidate hypothesis that deep mycorrhizal transitions frequently co-opted conserved fungal transmembrane nutrient-transport scaffolds rather than requiring radical active-site remodeling [13, 14, 15, 21, 23]. Functional transport kinetics remain to be tested experimentally in heterologous systems.

**Quaternary Rhizosphere Demography and Marker Resolution Across Mycorrhizal Taxa.** Across 383 conspecific sequences in 12 fungal populations, regional nuclear ITS and 28S LSU skylines capture Holocene agricultural and boreal expansion signals that slow-evolving 18S SSU rDNA (pi = 0.0000 in R. irregularis Cohort L5) cannot resolve [17, 20]. The multi-cluster ITS networks in R. irregularis (12 clusters, pi = 0.1083) and A. muscaria (4 clusters, pi = 0.0120) reflect contrasting dispersal ecology between soil-borne multinucleate AM spores and wind-dispersed boreal ECM basidiospores [13].

**Study Limitations.** Several methodological constraints qualify these inferences. First, mitochondrial COX1 dropped below the 10-taxon completeness threshold, leaving the 23-locus supermatrix entirely nuclear, and 21 sparse taxa failed the 55% site gate in concatenated chronogram estimation (though all 64 species were retained in quartet coalescent analyses). Second, conspecific Bayesian skylines rely on single-locus ITS or LSU/COX1 cohorts from heterogeneous public submissions rather than phased whole-genome resequencing. Third, structural threading evaluates a single static inward-occluded 4J05 crystal conformer without molecular dynamics simulations or biochemical transport assays; accordingly, evolutionary rates, introgression contrasts, and structural contacts are reported as candidate statistical correlations.
manuscript_prose.abstract_context: Resolving single versus multiple origins of mycorrhizal symbioses across the fungal tree of life.
manuscript_prose.executive_summary_lead: tracks 23 conserved nuclear loci, symbiotic nutrient-transporter remodeling, and root-associated diversification across 64 fungal species
manuscript_prose.latex_intro: Partitioned 23-locus nuclear phylogenomics, 64-species quartet coalescent inference, transporter codon selection, and conspecific population skylines across the fungal tree of life.
manuscript_prose.abstract_override: Mycorrhizal fungi sustain terrestrial plant nutrition through ancient arbuscular mutualisms in Glomeromycotina and Mucoromycotina alongside younger ectomycorrhizal and ericoid lineages in Ascomycota and Basidiomycota. However, deep fungal phylogenomics faces adenine-thymine compositional drift and long-branch attraction across early-diverging clades. Analyzing 489 curated NCBI sequences across 64 fungal species spanning all seven major compartments, we evaluated a completeness-gated 23-locus nuclear supermatrix (36,208 aligned columns across 43 species), 24-gene-tree quartet multispecies coalescent reconciliation (3,244,416 quartets), Goldman-Yang codon selection on 42 transporter and chitin-synthase orthologs threaded onto Serendipita indica PiPT (PDB 4J05), and 12 single-species coalescent skylines (383 isolates). Per-locus partitioned RY3 modeling reduced compositional skew (RCFV) by 87.1% to 0.0127 and improved maximum-likelihood fit by +5,836.89 nats over unpartitioned analysis, recovering all major symbiotic clades across ML (89-100% bootstrap) and quartet coalescent trees (Q = 0.7065). Autocorrelated relaxed-clock dating places crown Glomeromycotina at 413.2 Ma (365.2-438.2 Ma) and Mucoromycotina at 499.3 Ma (462.2-529.9 Ma), versus Dikarya ectomycorrhizal crown diversification in Agaricomycetes at 267.2 Ma (252.6-307.6 Ma). Strong purifying constraint (M0 dN/dS = 0.0660-0.1306) and 0.424 A structural conservation on PiPT 4J05 (Asn431-phosphate distance 3.39 A) align with repeated evolutionary recruitment of conserved nutrient-symport machinery across independent fungal transitions.
